# Opal Pettigrew

## Overview

- **Age:** Seventeen years old by the end of Volume 2  <sub>[v1 c15 P11](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0011), [v1 c15 P15](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0015), [v1 c30 P15](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0015)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c11 P11](../source/v01-c11.md#nw-v01-c11-p0011)</sub>
- **Status:** Deceased  <sub>[v3 c14 P0](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0000), [v3 c14 P30](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0030)</sub>
- **Origin:** Brierley  <sub>[v1 c11 P18](../source/v01-c11.md#nw-v01-c11-p0018), [v1 c15 P8](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0008)</sub>
- **Role:** Student and aspiring teacher  <sub>[v1 c15 P8](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0008), [v1 c30 P15](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0015)</sub>

## Appearance

Opal is a very attractive girl with a radiant, flushed complexion, big vivid blue eyes, and long blonde hair. She is tall, full-figured, and has a striking appearance. Towards the end of her life, her face grows pale and thin, her blue eyes shine with a feverish intensity, and her hands become delicate and almost transparent.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P11](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0011), [v1 c25 P1](../source/v01-c25.md#nw-v01-c25-p0001), [v1 c25 P28](../source/v01-c25.md#nw-v01-c25-p0028), [v1 c31 P4](../source/v01-c31.md#nw-v01-c31-p0004), [v3 c11 P4](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0004), [v3 c14 P5](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0005)_

## Personality

Opal is cheerful, sunny, and loves to laugh, but she is also prone to emotional outbursts, tears, and sentimentality. She has an intense obsession with romances, boys, and suitors, constantly boasting about her admirers and flirtations. Though sometimes perceived as vain or silly, she possesses a deeply affectionate nature and clings desperately to life and her friends when facing tragedy.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P11](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0011), [v1 c15 P28](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0028), [v1 c15 P39](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0039), [v1 c18 P15](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0015), [v1 c26 P21](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0021), [v1 c34 P21](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0021), [v1 c35 P1](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0001), [v1 c35 P3](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0003), [v3 c14 P5](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0005), [v3 c14 P11](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0011), [v3 c14 P17](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0017)_

## Goals

- To enjoy life, have many suitors, and eventually marry  <sub>[v1 c18 P15](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0015), [v1 c26 P21](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0021), [v1 c30 P15](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0015), [v3 c14 P17](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0017)</sub>
- To qualify as a teacher at Regent's Academy  <sub>[v1 c30 P15](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0015)</sub>
- To survive her illness and continue living  <sub>[v1 c31 P5](../source/v01-c31.md#nw-v01-c31-p0005), [v3 c14 P11](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0011), [v3 c14 P15](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0015)</sub>

## History

Opal attended Brierley school, where she sat in the fourth and fifth books alongside Nell Harcourt and Isolde Pembroke. She joined the school's story-writing club, where she gained a reputation for writing overly sentimental stories. After finishing school, she studied for the entrance examinations for Regent's Academy alongside her classmates and participated in a student concert, acting in the tableau 'Grace, Hope and Charity.' At Regent's Academy, she joined the Brierley student group and passed her examinations, qualifying for a First Class teaching license. Following a severe bout of congestion during her final winter at college, Opal's health rapidly declined into galloping consumption, preventing her from taking a teaching position at Pale Sands. She spent her final summer at her family's home in Brierley, continually denying the severity of her illness while remaining obsessed with her various suitors. After a frank, emotional conversation about her fears of death with Nell, Opal passed away peacefully in her sleep toward the end of summer.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P8](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0008), [v1 c15 P11](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0011), [v1 c15 P28](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0028), [v1 c24 P10](../source/v01-c24.md#nw-v01-c24-p0010), [v1 c24 P14](../source/v01-c24.md#nw-v01-c24-p0014), [v1 c26 P20](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0020), [v1 c26 P21](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0021), [v1 c30 P15](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0015), [v1 c30 P20](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0020), [v1 c32 P16](../source/v01-c32.md#nw-v01-c32-p0016), [v1 c32 P42](../source/v01-c32.md#nw-v01-c32-p0042), [v1 c34 P11](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0011), [v3 c11 P4](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0004), [v3 c11 P5](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0005), [v3 c14 P5](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0005), [v3 c14 P11](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0011), [v3 c14 P17](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0017), [v3 c14 P30](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0030)_

- Member of the Pettigrew family of Brierley  <sub>[v1 c15 P8](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0008), [v1 c25 P25](../source/v01-c25.md#nw-v01-c25-p0025)</sub>

## Quotes

> I really wish those two boys had stayed away tonight, because I was hoping we could have a wonderful, long conversation, Nell, so I could share so many things with you. The two of us have always been great friends, haven’t we?  <sub>[v3 c11 P53](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0053)</sub>

> The time is drawing near when I will be resting in that place. You, Isolde, and everyone else will be moving around, brimming with vitality—while I will be situated there—within the ancient cemetery—deceased!  <sub>[v3 c14 P6](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0006)</sub>

> And, oh, Nell... dying is not what I want. The thought of dying frightens me.  <sub>[v3 c14 P7](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0007)</sub>

> I want to live. I want to live the way other girls do. I—I desire to get married, Nell—and—and—possess tiny children.  <sub>[v3 c14 P17](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0017)</sub>

> I am pleased that I have shared this with you, Nell. Simply expressing everything has brought me relief.  <sub>[v3 c14 P18](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0018)</sub>
